# 65.23 Biblical Record: They Have Moses and the Prophets

Luke 16:29–31, in the rich man’s plea that Lazarus be sent to his brothers, locates the sufficient written witness: “They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.” When the plea is raised — if one went from the dead, they will repent — the answer is: “If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.”

The passage is used as record of rank, not as a second resurrection-file (Chapter 46 remains in force and is not retried). The writing already in hand is treated as the appointed written measure. A later spectacular sign is not granted as a higher court over that writing. The point is not that signs never occur. The point is that refusal of the writing is not cured by a replacement court of the extraordinary.

The gate uses the passage with control. Moses and the prophets are the earlier body already standing as Scripture (Chapter 51). Later apostolic writings stand continuous with that body (Chapters 50–54). The passage does not, in this file, deny later Scripture. It exhibits the principle the later writings themselves inherit: the written deposit is the measure; a later marvel is not, by being a marvel, a higher writing.

Thus:

> **Luke 16:29–31 exhibits written sufficiency as measure. The extraordinary is not granted as a court above the writing they already have.**

# 65.24 Biblical Record: Search the Scriptures

John 5:39 records His charge: “Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.” John 5:46–47 adds: had they believed Moses, they would have believed Him; if they believe not Moses’ writings, how shall they believe His words? The scriptures already stand as searchable testimony. His words do not abolish those writings. Unbelief toward the writings and unbelief toward Him are exhibited as one refusal.

In Acts 17 the writings are searched in truth and confirm the proclamation. The writing is the measure in both. The reader’s use may be false or true. The writing’s standing is not created by the use.

The gate uses the scenes as record of the first two operations named in the locked assignment: known and tested. The scriptures are to be searched. Claims are to be tested by them. The present file does not write the later discipline of interpretation (Chapter 84). It names the object of the search.

> **Searching the scriptures is the record’s own account of written measure in use. The use may fail. The standing of the writing does not fail with the use.**

# 65.25 Biblical Record: All Scripture Profitable

2 Timothy 3:15–17, already the principal inspiration-text, is used here as record of the operations taught, discerned, and lived, without a second inspiration-file.

# 65.26 Biblical Record: Received as the Word of God

1 Thessalonians 2:13 records right classification: “when ye received the word of God which ye heard of us, ye received it not as the word of men, but as it is in truth, the word of God, which effectually worketh also in you that believe.”

Chapter 64 already used the verse as neighbouring classification-record of the word as truth. The present file uses it as record of rank. Reception as the word of men and reception as the word of God are two different standings. Primary written authority is the written form of the second standing, already identified as Graphē. A later commentary remains the word of a man about that word, useful insofar as it conforms, not primary by being published.

The verse also joins “in truth” to effectual working in those who believe. Lived operation is not a second source. It is the word working as what it is. The reconstructible proposition that experience pillows in the Graphē’s truth belongs here as coherence with this classification, not as a later licence, and not as “the source says.”

Thus:

> **1 Thessalonians 2:13 records the classification the gate requires: not as men’s word, but as it is in truth God’s word. Later human writings do not inherit that classification by discussing it.**

# 65.27 Biblical Record: Do Not Add, Do Not Diminish

Deuteronomy 4:2 commands: “Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish ought from it.” Deuteronomy 12:32 repeats the fence. Proverbs 30:5–6 joins the purity of His word to the warning: “Add thou not unto his words, lest he reprove thee, and thou be found a liar.” Revelation 22:18–19, at the close of the later testimony, warns against adding to and taking from the words of the prophecy of that book.

The texts are used as record of rank, not as a closed mechanical table of sixty-six titles constructed in this file, and not as Chapter 52 retried. A word that may not be added to or diminished from is not one written authority among equals. Equals may be supplemented by further equals. The writing fenced against addition and diminution is the measure of later speech about it.

The fence does not, here, become a claim that no later Scripture could be given after Deuteronomy. Later Scripture was given, and has been identified as continuous testimony (Chapters 50–54). The fence is the principle of rank: later speech does not sit above the word as a higher court; later Scripture, where given, stands as further Graphē, not as a human supplement that judges the former word. Human addition remains the warned act.

Thus:

> **The fence against adding and diminishing is biblical record of primary written measure. Later human speech is not granted as a court above the word.**

# 65.28 Reconstructing the Aletheia Proposition: Conformity Pillows in the Graphē

A reconstructible proposition from the project’s own doctrinal materials states that true experience in conformity with Christ pillows in the unleavened sincerity and truth of the Graphē — Holy Writ as writings of unchallenged standing — whether for persons, organizations, governments, or nations; and that this writing is the premiere convention for hearing from God, as distinct from analogical nonliteral religious substitutes.

The proposition is not adopted as “the source says.” It is tested.

**What is claimed.** Experience that is truly in conformity with Christ is governed by the Graphē’s truth, not by a substitute that will not sit under the writing.

**What the claim means.** “Pillows in” names dependence and rest: the experience takes its measure from the writing. “Unleavened sincerity and truth” names the writing’s character, not sincerity as the definition of truth. Chapter 64 already distinguished those.

**Premises.** The Father’s word is truth (Chapter 64). The writing cannot be broken because of what it is (Chapter 63). The Truth treats the writing as court (Chapters 59–61). The writing is God-breathed Holy Writ of the God who cannot lie (Chapters 10–12, 30–31, 51–58).

**Biblical correspondence.** John 17:17; John 8:31–32; 1 Thessalonians 2:13; Isaiah 8:20; John 10:35. The correspondence holds.

**What follows.** The proposition coheres with the gate: primary written authority is the standing such experience requires. Organizations and nations are not excluded from the measure by being large. Labels are not the measure.

**What does not follow here.** That the First Principles have been taught. That *apeiros* and *spoudazō* have been examined. That every later practice calling itself Christian is thereby certified. That sincerity is truth. Those remain later or already refused.

Thus:

> **The reconstructible proposition is received as coherence with the gate, not as a substitute for the join, and not as Movement IX or the First Principles written now.**

# 65.29 Reconstructing the Bible-Introduction Proposition: What the Writing Is as Measure

A reconstructible proposition from the Bible Introduction materials states that the Bible is God’s inspired revelation of origin and destiny, His will to men, the record of His dealings, not an amulet that works by mere presence, not a book that says one thing and means another as its ordinary mode, not a fetish, and that its teachings are to be studied and practiced; and that “all Scripture,” not a part, is given by inspiration of God.

The proposition is not adopted as “the source says.” It is tested.

**What is claimed.** The writing is revelation-record and will, to be used as such, not as a charm, and inspiration’s scope is all Scripture.

**Premises already in force.** Chapters 15–22 defined the Bible and the Graphē. Chapters 30–31 established inspiration and “all.” Chapter 56 established guarantees. Chapter 57 established non-failure as record. Chapter 64 identified the word as truth.

**What follows for the gate.** A writing that is revelation-record, not a charm, is used as measure by being read, tested, reasoned through, taught, discerned, and lived — the locked assignment’s own list. A charm would be primary as object-magic. The Graphē is primary as truthful writing. The Introduction’s refusal of the amulet is therefore coherence with this chapter’s definition of written authority, not a rival definition.

**What does not follow here.** That every later note in a study edition inherits the writing’s standing. That literal sense, already a methodological preference in those materials, has been rewritten as this file’s complete hermeneutic. Movement X remains the labour-file.

Thus:

> **The reconstructible Introduction proposition is received as coherence: the writing is measure by what it is, not by charm, and “all Scripture” remains unweakened. Notes about the writing are not the writing.**

# 65.30 Distinctions Required by the Conclusion

The conclusion requires four distinctions already named as objects and now stated as required by the verdict.

**This chapter is not the end of the book.** Movement VIII closes. Movements IX–X remain. The First Principles remain. A finished gate is the condition of later work, not the abolition of later work.

**Primary written authority is not the authority of every interpretation.** The text stands. The reading may fail. Foreshadow of Movement IX is a limit of the doctrine. It is not Movement IX.

**Primary written authority is not a blank check for tradition.** Tradition may serve. It does not, by serving, become the Graphē or a court above it.

**Using earlier files is not rewriting them.** The John 10 arc remains Chapters 59–63. The identification remains Chapter 64. The Movement VII synthesis remains Chapter 58. The lexical files remain Chapters 20–22. The present function is the join those files warrant as rank.

A fifth distinction belongs with them because the word “primary” invites it:

**Primary among written authorities is not the claim that God has never spoken except in this corpus, and not the claim that no other writing exists.** Rank is the verdict. Ontology of all speech and of all paper is not the verdict.

Thus:

> **The distinctions are the verdict’s shape. They prevent the gate from becoming a slogan that finishes the book, baptizes readers, or crowns tradition.**

The Bible-first methodology itself distinguished establishing the text’s authority from the later hermeneutical question: once we have an authoritative truthful text, how do we correctly understand it? That later question is not this question.

If the book ended here, the Truth’s writing would have been ranked and still left unexamined as a mishandled object. Interpreters would be undistinguished as a dedicated problem. Diligence would remain an English moral, not σπουδάζω examined. The First Principles would be asked to rest on a gate that had been named and then treated as if naming abolished the need to enter.

Closure of Movement VIII is success of this file. Closure of the manuscript is not this file’s office.

# 65.32 Primary Written Authority ≠ Every Interpretation Authoritative

The reduction says:

Chapter 58 already attached standing to the writing, not to the interpreter. Chapter 64 already refused to confer “thy word is truth” upon every later quotation.

The present file must already refuse the transfer, or the gate would be a blank check. The refusal is not Movement IX. Movement IX will examine how the transfer occurs, how readings fail, how systems replace the text, how tergiversation works, how heresies become accepted, how aridity and *apeiros* arise. The present file names the ranking that makes those later analyses necessary: if the writing is primary, a failed reading is a failed reading, not a second Graphē.

God true, man fallible, remains the ranking. The ranking is not contempt for teaching. Teachers are commanded. They remain under the writing they teach.

Thus:

> **The gate does not baptize interpreters. The writing is primary. The reading is accountable. Dedicated examination of mishandling remains later.**

# 65.33 Primary Written Authority ≠ Blank Check for Tradition

The reduction says:

# 65.35 Competing Claim: Tradition or Institution as Higher Court

The reduction says:

The reduction fails.

If institution were the higher court, Isaiah 8:20 would send the people to the office rather than to the law and the testimony. The Bereans would be ignoble for searching the scriptures whether an apostolic sermon were so. 1 Thessalonians 2:13 would classify the word as the word of the institution rather than as it is in truth the word of God. The record does not say those things.

The reduction often presents itself as a defence of order. Order is not under attack. Office is not being abolished. Rank is being stated. An office that serves the Graphē is in its place. An office that claims to be the Graphē’s higher court has claimed what the join does not grant.

Unverifiable stories of a particular council inventing the Bible as a library are not used here as premises. Chapter 52 already refused Nicaea-as-canon-origin as an unverified origin-story. The present file does not invent a replacement story. It uses the order already earned: standing, then receiving, then listing.

Thus:

> **Making tradition or institution primary over the Graphē fails. Recognition is not creation. Office is not the higher court. The writing remains the measure of the office.**

The reduction says:

# 65.39 Reason Through the Evidence

The inference can now be exhibited.

**Premise 1.** God is the ground of truth and cannot lie; genuine divine communication is not His falsehood (Chapters 10–12, used not retried).

**Premise 2.** God has made known; that making-known has been authenticated as given (Chapters 13, 23–42, 55, used not retried).

**Premise 3.** All Scripture is God-breathed as writing; inspiration warrants truthfulness of the record according to what it actually communicates; the record does not fail as that writing (Chapters 30–31, 56–57, used not retried).

**Premise 4.** This corpus has been identified, recognized, and grounded as Scripture, one written testimony, with authority as the written Word at the Movement VII level (Chapters 51–58, used not retried).

**Premise 5.** The Truth appeals to what is written as the court of a capital dispute; the Graphē is court, not decoration (Chapters 59–61, used not retried).

**Premise 6.** The scripture cannot be broken because of what it is: God’s truthful written Word, such that its force as court cannot be loosed without denying that identity (Chapters 62–63, used not retried).

**Premise 7.** The Father’s word is truth; sanctification through truth is through that word because that word is truth (Chapter 64, used not retried).

**Premise 8.** Truth is not sincerity, not usefulness, not institutional consensus; the thing described is not the description of the thing; later speech about the word is not the word (Chapters 1–3, 14, 58, used not retried).

**Inference.** Therefore the Graphē is the primary written authority by which truth is known, tested, reasoned through, taught, discerned, and lived: the decisive written measure among written authorities, not one religious book among equals, not subordinate to later tradition or institution as a higher court, not interchangeable with every later claim about the text. “Primary” names that rank. It does not name the non-existence of other writings, the infallibility of interpreters, a blank check for tradition, the end of the book, or the later files. The investigator is warranted, with full force, in receiving this as Movement VIII’s last word. Movement IX remains the next question.

**Alternative explanations refused.** That tradition or institution is the higher court. That private experience is primary. That the Graphē is one religious book among equals. That this file is already Movement IX, Movement X, or the First Principles. That this file is Chapter 64 retried or Chapter 58 rewritten. That “primary” means no other writing exists. That the gate baptizes every interpretation. Those alternatives fail the join, the biblical record of measuring-function, and the premises already in force.

Thus:

> **The inference is inspectable. The gate follows from the conjunction of members already earned. The alternatives fail as accounts of that conjunction.**

# 65.40 Explicit Versus Inferred

**Explicit.** The Son asks whether it is not written in their law. He cites “I said, Ye are gods.” He says the scripture cannot be broken. He prays, “Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.” All Scripture is given by inspiration of God and is profitable for doctrine, reproof, correction, and instruction in righteousness. Isaiah sends a people to the law and to the testimony. The Bereans search the scriptures whether those things were so. Moses and the prophets are named as the writing they already have. The word is received not as the word of men but as it is in truth the word of God. The word is fenced against adding and diminishing.

**Inferred, as warranted.** That “primary written authority” names the Graphē’s firstness among written measures for knowing, testing, reasoning through, teaching, discerning, and living truth. That the seven members jointly warrant that rank. That tradition, institution, and private experience are not higher courts. That the Graphē is not one religious book among equals. That interpreters are not, by interpreting, the measure. That other writings exist and remain secondary. That Movement VIII is complete as assigned.

**Not inferred here.** Movement IX’s dedicated mishandling analysis. Movement X’s labour-files. *Spoudazō* as this file’s object. *Apeiros* as this file’s object. The Six First Principles as content. Physical indestructibility of every later copy. Infallibility of every interpreter. A reconstructed council inventing the Bible. Unverifiable imprimatur-offices as if they were in the text. The end of the book.

The line is the difference between a gate-file and a later-file. Crossing it would be theft. Refusing to infer what the conjunction warrants would be under-claim. # 65.41 The Warranted Conclusion Stated with Full Force

The investigator is warranted, with full force, in receiving this conclusion:

> **The Graphē is the primary written authority by which truth is known, tested, reasoned through, taught, discerned, and lived.**

The Graphē is the decisive written measure — not merely one religious book among equals, not subordinate to later tradition or institution as a higher court, not interchangeable with every later claim about the text.

The warrant is the conjunction already named. The God who cannot lie has made known. That making-known has been authenticated as given. All Scripture is God-breathed writing that does not fail as truthful divine writing of what it actually communicates. This corpus has been identified, recognized, and grounded as Scripture, with standing as the written Word already earned. The Truth has appealed to what is written as court. The writing cannot be broken because of what it is. The Son has identified the Father’s word as truth. Therefore this writing is the primary written authority for the operations the locked assignment names.

“Primary” means first among written authorities for those operations. It does not mean that no other writing exists. It does not mean that interpreters are infallible. It does not mean that the book is finished. It does not mean a blank check for tradition. Those limits are the shape of the doctrine. They are not a delayed doubt about the doctrine.

The biblical record of measuring-function confirms the join without replacing it: “it is written”; to the law and to the testimony; they have Moses and the prophets; search the scriptures; all Scripture profitable; received not as the word of men but as it is in truth the word of God; do not add and do not diminish. Rival speech, later marvel, later office, and present impression are not granted as higher courts.

Competing reductions fail. Tradition or institution as higher court fails the order already earned. Private experience as primary fails the court of John 10 and the sufficiency named in Luke 16. One religious book among equals fails the investigation as conducted. This chapter as already Movement IX, Movement X, or the First Principles fails the locked assignments.

The investigator is therefore warranted, with full force, in receiving Movement VIII’s last word as drawn. The Graphē-gate is in force. Sequence continues. Sequence is not hesitation.

Thus:

> **The Graphē is the primary written authority. The conclusion is the conjunction of members already earned, exhibited in the record’s own measuring-grammar, and fenced against the live reductions. Movement VIII is complete.**

The governing authorial maxim remains:

> **Do not merely tell the reader what to conclude.**
>
> **Give the reader the definitions, evidence, biblical record, reasoning, distinctions, and inferential steps necessary to see why the conclusion follows.**

And:

> **Do not make the reader choose between reason and Scripture. Teach the reader to reason through Scripture.**

This chapter has defined primary written authority as the Graphē’s firstness among written measures for knowing, testing, reasoning through, teaching, discerning, and living truth. It has distinguished that object from a second identification-file, from Chapter 58 rewritten, from the end of the book, from interpreter-infallibility, from a blank check for tradition, from every later religious writing, from the claim that no other writing exists, from Movement IX, from Movement X, and from the First Principles. It has used premises already in force and refused premises that remain later. It has given one clean account of sequence and limits. It has defined authority, written, and primary. It has named the six functions. It has stated the positive warrant as conjunction. It has exhibited the biblical record of measuring-function. It has refused the live reductions. It has distinguished the explicit from the inferred.

The Easton test has been applied in its proper analogue. A later writer may say that the Bible is one classic among others, or that the church is the higher court, or that experience is the court, or that the gate is already mishandling and already the First Principles, or that “primary” means no other book exists, or that every interpretation is as binding as the text. The manuscript has not accepted those sentences as premises. It has asked what the writing is, what the preceding argument has earned, and what the record actually warrants.

Circularity has been refused. The argument is not: the Bible is primary because the Bible says it is primary; therefore interpreters and traditions are infallible; therefore the book is finished. The argument is: the Speaker cannot lie; He has made known; the making-known has been authenticated; the writing is God-breathed and does not fail as record; this is the corpus; the Truth has used it as court; it cannot be loosed because of what it is; that word is truth; therefore this writing is the decisive written measure.

Prematurity has been refused. The chapter has not consumed Movement IX, Movement X, or the First Principles.

Duplication has been refused. Identification remains Chapter 64. Why remains Chapter 63. Sense remains Chapter 62. Logic remains Chapter 61. Psalm remains Chapter 60. Scene remains Chapter 59. Synthesis remains Chapter 58. Lexical establishment remains Chapters 20–22. Truth’s definition remains Chapters 1–3. God’s truthfulness remains Chapters 10–12. The present function is the dedicated gate, and the close the locked guidance names.

Source-integration has been performed without “the source says.” The reconstructible proposition that experience in conformity with Christ is governed by the Graphē’s truth has been tested as coherence with the gate. The reconstructible Introduction proposition that the writing is revelation-record rather than charm, and that all Scripture is inspired, has been tested as coherence with written measure. Neither has been treated as a licence, and neither has been treated as Movement IX or the First Principles.

Thus:

> **The standard has been applied: the Graphē has been shown to be the primary written authority as the conclusion earned by the preceding argument, not announced as a slogan, and not postponed as if the gate were weak.**

# 65.44 From Primary Written Authority to When Authoritative Truth Is Mishandled

A gate, now controlled as the Graphē’s firstness among written measures, still leaves a further question.

The gate-file is in force. The Graphē is the primary written authority by which truth is known, tested, reasoned through, taught, discerned, and lived. The writing is the decisive written measure. Those sentences are the cleared ground. They are not yet the dedicated examination of what happens when that authority is mishandled: when the authority of the text is confused with the authority of the interpretation; when the writing is misread; when theology, philosophy, tradition, and institution take the writing’s place; when secondary sources become primary; when tergiversation turns aside; when heresies become accepted; when reasonability dries; when the reader is *apeiros* — unskillful in the word.

If the gate were not named, the next question would still be why this writing is the primary written authority. The gate has been named. If this chapter were already that later examination, the next file would be repetition. This chapter is not that later examination. The next question is therefore the construction the locked assignment names: Authority of Scripture Versus Authority of Interpretation — Movement IX opens.

That is the proper open of the next chapter. Primary written authority was never meant to be a slogan that finishes the book, and it was never meant to baptize every later reading. It was meant to be the rank of the writing as measure, sufficient to justify taking the next question, which is the question a ranked writing itself forces once the rank has been named: how is the authority of the text to be distinguished from the fallibility of the interpreter?

The next file must not steal this gate as if primary written authority had not been drawn. This file must not steal that distinction as if Movement IX were already written. Naming the neighbourhood is not performing the examination.
